Kul ḥa kəmšayəʕ i barṯo, kəmšayəʕ aʕma hadiye, mənayye fanera, mənayye kallat, mənayye gurwe, mənayye šarpat, mənayye fəṣeṭən, kul ḥa lu goran du xaṭər, d kətla li kalayo sədayye. Hani aq qarye dab bə babe di kalo. W kəmmila i ṣabaḥiye, koṯən l bə ḥaṯno.
data.translation: Was tun sie nun am Morgen? Die Eltern der Braut sind damit beschäftigt, ein Essen für die Braut zu machen, das man ṣăbaḥiye (Morgenmahlzeit) nennt. Jeder entsprechend seinen Möglichkeiten. Was machen die Gäste der Braut? Jeder schickt seine Tochter und schickt mit ihr ein Geschenk, manche einen Pullover, manche Geld, manche Strümpfe, manche Kopftücher, manche Röcke, jeder gemäß dem Ansehen, das die Braut bei ihnen genießt. Das sind die Gäste der Brauteltern. Man nennt es die Morgenmahlzeit, sie kommen zum Haus des Bräutigams.

rationale: Thin II.2 Infectum cell; food preparation with context for recipient or cooking process.

data.translation: Von Sonntag bis Mittwoch. Wenn es Mittwochabend geworden ist, folgt etwas, das man radde nennt. Die Eltern der Braut bereiten ein Essen für Braut und Bräutigam vor, und ein Geschenk für den Bräutigam, und sie kommen abends, am Vorabend des Donnerstags, am Mittwoch, laden sie ein und sagen: Wir möchten, dass ihr zu uns kommt.

data.turoyo: <...> Kəmḥaḏ̣rile darbo d nofəq w məǧġəl ba ṭboʕe w frose.
data.translation: 1) Turkey gave Father Aziz support, so that he would become head of the Syriac Orthodox Church in all Turkey. They prepare a way for him to come out and speak in print and publications.

rationale: Figurative path as opportunity, overt beneficiary -le and following d-clause; one clear attestation. Permitted glossary search mḥaḏ found no corresponding collocation.

summary: I distinguishes arrival/becoming ready in finite forms from presence/readiness in Part act.; invariant Arabic-shaped ḥaḏ̣ər/ḥaḏ̣ir and audience plurals remain outside secure native boxes.

II has zero-marked patients, object suffixes and beneficiary l-suffixes; active ruḥo constructions are compositional reflexives, not new idiomatic phrases. The Detransitive can alternate with an explicit reflexive object (53/143).

The cross-referenced ḥyḏ̣r entry was consulted with the permitted lookup: it contains overlapping unexpanded mḥaḏ̣alle/mḥaḏ̣ər material. Preserve both entries pending editorial reconciliation; do not move examples solely by spelling.
Infectum-wa spans recurrent cooking and construction work. Routine counts especially support frequent I Part act. presence/readiness; their 37 occurrences require no individual decisions.
Existing II.2 wording, including its editorial question, is retained. Assembly and readiness do not by themselves prove lexical cooking.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce provides no edition translation. English in the input is machine translation and is not quoted as an edition translation. Added examples therefore have an empty translation field; meanings are assessed from the Turoyo.
I ḥuḏarwo/ḥuḏ̣arwo contrasts with ḥaḏərwo/ḥaḏəriwo and ḥaḏərinawo; habitual attendance favours Infectum-wa for the former. Preterit-wa does not on its own entail an English pluperfect.

Current-presence plural ḥaḏiri and second-plural ḥaḏiritu retain qaṭəl-shaped endings, whereas ready-state ḥaḏərto yo and ḥaḏ̣ire have Part act. morphology. Preserve the glossary boxes while recording aspectual overlap.

Plain ḏ, emphatic ḏ̣ and u/ə/a alternations coexist in the transcribed interviews; this input is not uniformly learned written prose. The overlapping ḥyḏ̣r entry remains an editorial issue inherited from round 1.
ḥəḏoro (Jan 1.6/96) may be learned nominal vocabulary, but is not secure evidence for a new II Infinitiv box. ḥəḏḏar (Jan 2.35/5533) is similarly withheld from Part act.

summary: Readiness has inanimate subjects (dough, food, building materials); presence at a funeral is expressed with b-. Neither participant change requires a separate numbered sense.
Patients include brides, soldiers, equipment, dough and grain; food preparation can precede actual cooking, so a food object alone does not force sense 2.

Attendance at congresses, church rites and television discussions extends the round-1 presence-at-event pattern; b- remains common, while Jan 1.39/1739 has a zero-marked event noun. No separate participation sense is needed.
Books, broadcasts, military preparations and winter supplies are preparation patients. Reflexive ruḥo remains compositional and supports round 1, without a new sense.
